info.description: Production Base URL to be used during implementation: {your company workspace subdomain}.talkpush.com/api/talkpush_services With the Talkpush APIs you can instantly plug your lead source into out platform to enjoy the benefits of Talkpush. You can also synch your existing HR / Recruitment technology stack with your Talkpush account. To be able to use our API you will need pass an api key as a parameter for each API call. In case you do not know your current API key you can contact our support team at cs@talkpush.com.

tags.name: Candidate Attributes API
tags.description: List and create candidate (lead) custom attribute definitions at the company level. Definitions appear in the recruiter UI and can be written on leads via the `others` field using the attribute key. Both built-in (`default`) and custom attributes are returned on list.

tags.name: Agents API
tags.description: Collection of endpoints related to AI Agents (SmartCall Settings). Agents are configurable AI-powered voice/interview agents that can be linked to campaigns, question sets, and candidate attribute extractions.

tags.name: Labels API
tags.description: Collection of endpoints related to candidate labels. Labels are simple, company-wide tags that recruiters use to flag and filter candidates (for example: "Priority", "Referral", "Needs Review"). The same labels are visible in the Talkpush UI; anything added via the API immediately appears in the UI and on the candidate's `labels` field returned by the Leads API.

tags.name: Message Templates API
tags.description: Endpoints for managing Message Templates — the structured, token-based messages used by autoflows and integrations for standardised communications (interview invitations, rejection notices, offer letters, onboarding instructions). Templates are returned and accepted with content in Handlebars format (e.g. `{{candidate_name}}`), regardless of how they are stored internally. Use `GET /messaging/tokens` to discover the full list of tokens available in your company.

tags.name: Tokens API
tags.description: Endpoint for discovering the message tokens available for use inside Message Templates. Returns both system-level reserved tokens (e.g. `candidate_name`, `job_title`) and any custom tokens configured for the company.

tags.name: Movement Reasons API
tags.description: Endpoint for listing the company's candidate movement reasons — the configurable Shortlist Reasons and Reject Reasons that recruiters select when shortlisting or rejecting a candidate. Use these IDs/names to mirror reason labels in external dashboards or to map them back to Talkpush when syncing status changes.

tags.name: Managers API
tags.description: Endpoint for listing the company's managers (platform users with role-based permissions). Use the returned IDs to discover valid managers before assigning them to campaign permissions, targeting them in automation, or mirroring the user directory in external tools. Read-only; results are scoped to the authenticated tenant and exclude deactivated managers.

get.summary: Retrieve a list of leads matching your search criterias
get.description:
This API endpoint will enable you to search through your lead database programatically  with the same criterias than you would use on the recruiter's leads page.  You can execute 2 kinds of search: 
  * Use the query parameter which is equivalent to typing your search query in a search bar. 
  * Use a combination of parameter to execute an advanced search

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: The API key provided for your application

parameters.name: filter[query]
parameters.description: Search keywords like application id filter[query]='AP123'. Other search keywords like name, email or phone number.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number of lead list to return.

parameters.name: filter[campaign_id]
parameters.description: Campaign id of the campaign.

parameters.name: filter[campaign_id][]
parameters.description: The result will have all leads listed in all said campaigns. This parameter may be passed campaign_id divided by coma. filter[campaign_id]=1,2,3

parameters.name: filter[status_selected]
parameters.description: This parameter is used to filter the leads by current status. Only leads with a status equal to the filter provided will be returned. Valid statuses are 'pending', 'completed', 'shortlisted', 'on_hold', 'rejected', 'hired', 'no_response' or custom like 'custom_status'. Check the Folders API to get the valid list for the company.

parameters.name: filter[creation_start_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were created on or after the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[creation_end_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were created on or before the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[updated_start_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were updated on or after the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[updated_end_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were updated on or before the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[source_selected]
parameters.description: Search results will be filtered by provided source.

parameters.name: filter[location_selected]
parameters.description: Location filter for lead search results.

parameters.name: filter[location_radius_selected]
parameters.description: This will define a radius, in kilometers, from the location selected. All leads inside that radius will be included in the search results.

parameters.name: filter[label_selected]
parameters.description: The name of a label already created in the system. Search results will include all leads with this label.

parameters.name: filter[completion_method_selected]
parameters.description: Completion method of campaign invitation.

parameters.name: filter[resume_selected]
parameters.description: If attached is set, it will look for leads with resume. Values must be either 'attached' or 'not_attached'

parameters.name: filter[scheduled_at_start_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were scheduled on or after the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[scheduled_at_end_date]
parameters.description: Return leads that were scheduled on or before the provided date. Date format must be DD-MM-YYYY.

parameters.name: filter[sort_by_selected]
parameters.description: Sorting of lead results. Allowed values include 'name', 'source', 'location', 'created_at', 'completion_date'.

parameters.name: filter[others][custom_attribute]
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to filter with the custom candidate attributes from the Others fields(jsonb column). If the attribute record with 'custom_attribute' key exists, then the data type (number, text or date) linked to it is used for matching, if it does not exist then it defaults to text. Data types number or text are matched as equal to the value sent and the Date type (format dd-mm-yyyy) matches for a greater or equal value.

parameters.name: include_documents
parameters.description: Optional. If sent as true the documents linked to the leads are returned. Default to false.

parameters.name: include_answers
parameters.description: Optional. If sent as true the answers linked to the leads are returned. Default to false.

parameters.name: include_attachments
parameters.description: Optional. If sent as true the attachments linked to the leads are returned. Default to false.

200.description: All leads that match the entered query.

500.description: Internal server error, we will provide you with the exception message of the application.

patch.description:
Updates the details of an existing lead. In addition to the fields on the candidate, this endpoint accepts an optional `candidate.labels` object to add or remove labels on the candidate in a single request.

**Labels payload (optional):** When `candidate.labels` is provided, it MUST include both an `add` and a `remove` array (send an empty array if you don't need that side). All names referenced in `add`/`remove` must already exist as company labels (create them first via `POST /company/labels`); if any are missing the whole request fails with 422 and nothing is changed. Names that don't exist as labels yet cause the whole request to fail with **422**, and no labels are modified — the change is all-or-nothing.

get.summary: Retrieve the changelog for a specific agent
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of audit log entries for the given agent, ordered by most recent first. Each entry describes a single create, update, or destroy event — who made the change, when, and what fields were affected.

For `created` entries the `changes` array is always empty (the initial state is not diffed). For `updated` entries each item in `changes` names the API field that changed and includes both the previous and new value.

**Possible `field` values inside a change entry:**
- `agent_name` — display name of the agent (stored as `title`)
- `description` — short description
- `prompt` — agent prompt, rendered as a plain-text string
- `data_extractions` — array of `{ "candidate_attribute": "<key>" }` objects

is_active.description: Set to `true` to create the agent in active (published) state; `false` for inactive (draft). Defaults to inactive when omitted.

prompt.description: The agent's prompt. Supports Handlebars-style variables: `{{messenger_interview_url}}`, `{{interview_page_url}}`, `{{messenger_interview_link}}`.

data_extractions.description: List of data extraction rules to configure on the agent. Unlike the update endpoint (which uses `{ candidate_attribute: { id } }`), here `candidate_attribute` is the attribute **key** string as returned by the Candidate Attributes API.

candidate_attribute.description: The `key` of the candidate attribute to map the extracted value to (e.g. `"english_level"`). Use the Candidate Attributes API to look up valid keys.

data_type.description: Data type of the extracted value (e.g. `string`, `integer`).

description.description: Instructions to the AI on what to extract.

number_of_values.description: Expected number of values to extract. Defaults to the length of `allowed_values` when provided, otherwise 1.

allowed_values.description: Optional list of allowed values for the extraction. When provided, the extraction is constrained to these values and `number_of_values` defaults to their count.

agent_create_response.description: Response body returned after successfully creating an agent (HTTP 201). The `data_extractions` field is an array — unlike the keyed map returned by the show/update endpoints.

id.description: Unique identifier of the newly created agent.

description.description: Short description of the agent's purpose.

question_set_id.description: ID of the linked question set, if any.

provider_agent_id.description: The agent identifier on the external provider's platform.

data_extractions.description: List of data extraction rules configured on the agent.

id.description: ID of the candidate attribute record.

candidate_attribute.description: Key of the candidate attribute this extraction maps to.

data_type.description: Data type of the extracted value.

description.description: Instructions to the AI on what to extract.

allowed_values.description: List of allowed values for the extraction. Empty array if unconstrained.

is_active.description: `true` if the agent is active (published); `false` if inactive (draft).

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the agent was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the agent was last updated.

name.description: Display name; unique within the company.

updated_at.description: When the label was last updated.

name.description: Display name. Trimmed of surrounding whitespace. Must be unique within the company and cannot contain `,`, `#` or `?`.

message.example: A label with name Priority already exists.

message_template.description: A Message Template used by autoflows and integrations for standardised communications.

content.description: Template body in Handlebars format. Dynamic values are expressed as `{{token_name}}`.

type.description: The communication channel this template is designed for.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag for the template content (e.g. `en`, `fr`, `es`).

category.description: Free-form grouping that spans types, useful for organising templates by workflow stage (e.g. `onboarding`, `scheduling`, `rejection`, `offer`).

settings.description: Channel-specific settings (e.g. `subject_line` for email templates). The internal `content_state` key is always excluded.

tokens.description: List of tokens detected in the template content.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the template was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the template was last updated.

token.description: A message token available for use in template content.

id.description: The token key used in Handlebars syntax — use this as `{{id}}` in `content`.

display_name.description: Human-readable label shown in the UI.

description.description: Optional description of what the token resolves to at send time. `null` for system tokens.

content.description: Template body in Handlebars format. Use `{{token_id}}` for dynamic values (see `GET /messaging/tokens` for available tokens).

type.description: Communication channel. Must be one of `email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `messenger`. (`calendar` is not yet supported via the API.)

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag. Defaults to `en` when omitted.

settings.description: Optional channel-specific settings. For email templates, include `subject_line` here.

invalid_tokens.description: List of unrecognised token names found in `content`.

message_template_update_request.description: All fields are optional. Only provided fields are updated.

content.description: New content in Handlebars format. All tokens are re-validated if this field is present.

settings.description: Settings to merge into the existing settings object. `content_state` is always stripped.

movement_reason.description: A single movement reason — a configurable Shortlist or Reject reason used when changing a candidate's status.

id.description: Database id of the movement reason.

name.description: Display name of the reason in Title Case (the underlying stored name is converted, e.g. `failed_background_check` becomes `Failed Background Check`).

type.description: Bucket the reason belongs to. `rejected` corresponds to Reject Reasons; `shortlisted` corresponds to Shortlist Reasons.

message.example: Invalid type 'foo'. Must be one of: rejected, shortlisted.

manager.description: A single manager — a platform user belonging to the company, with a role and contact details.

name.description: Manager's full name (first and last name combined, trimmed). Falls back to the email address when no name is set.

role.description: Manager's resolved role name (e.g. `owner`, `manager`, `limited manager`, or a custom role).

status.description: Status of the job requisition. Only OPEN status is currently supported.

job_profile_id.description: Job Profile ID. This should be mapped to a Job Profile in Talkpush.

locale.description: Language/locale for the job posting. This should be configured in the company settings.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. This should be configured in the company settings.

long_description.description: Detailed job description. This can be a plain text or HTML string.

publish_on_job_listing_page.description: Whether to publish the job on the listing page

allow_reapplication.description: Allow re-application while current application is active
